ingredients.cook_qty: 1/4 cup, plus a handful for topping

instructions: Grind 1/4 cup of the bonito flakes to a fine powder in a spice grinder or with the back of a spoon in a bowl. Set aside.
Slice the scallions thinly, mince the 1 tbsp pickled ginger and cut the octopus into 1/2 inch pieces. Keep them in separate piles by the stove.
In a bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder and salt. Add the eggs, soy sauce and dashi, and whisk until smooth. Transfer the batter to a pitcher or measuring cup with a spout.
Heat a takoyaki pan over medium heat for a few minutes. Brush the 2 tbsp oil generously over every mold and the flat top.
Pour in the batter so the molds overflow a little. Add 1 to 3 pieces of octopus to each mold and sprinkle with the ground bonito.

Top with the tenkasu, scallions and minced ginger. After about 3 minutes, when the bottoms are set, use two skewers to cut the batter between the molds. Turn each ball a quarter turn, tucking the loose batter back in.
Cook for 4 minutes. Turn the balls again, moving them around so they brown evenly, and cook for 4 minutes, until they're golden and the centers are cooked through.
Transfer the takoyaki to a plate. Drizzle with the takoyaki sauce and the mayonnaise, then sprinkle with the aonori and a handful of bonito flakes.
Serve hot with extra pickled ginger. The centers stay very hot, so let them cool for a minute before the first bite.
method_notes: Both sources use a flour, egg and dashi batter poured into a takoyaki pan, with boiled octopus, tenkasu, scallion and pickled ginger inside. The lead adds baking powder for a lighter ball and ground bonito in each mold; the other source skips both and uses less flour. Both finish with sauce, mayonnaise, aonori and bonito flakes. You need a takoyaki pan for this one. Boiled octopus is sold ready to use at Japanese grocery stores.
